title: Adaptive benchmark oracle for early performance alerts in PR CI
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight, adaptive 'benchmark oracle' to PR CI that provides high-confidence early alerts for performance regressions (tokens/sec, p95 latency) without imposing large GPU/time costs on the PR pipeline. The oracle should combine fast synthetic microbench checks with history-aware statistical modeling to reduce false positives while still catching meaningful regressions before merge.

What success looks like:
- Detect >= 90% of production-impacting regressions surfaced by our nightly full-benchmark within 24 hours, with <= 5% false positive rate on PR checks after tuning.
- PR check latency added <= 2 minutes for the fast path and <= 25 minutes for the extended path (when run).
- Clear actionable feedback in PR: metric diffs by slice, confidence score, suggested mitigation (canary label/rollback/benchmarking link).

Design summary:
1) Two-tier approach: 
   - Fast synthetic microbench (30–120s): run a small set of curated traces (mini-seed) against the changed runtime codepaths on a single small-GPU worker. Measure tokens/sec and p95 on a short warmup + steady window. Purpose: quick triage for large regressions.
   - Adaptive shadow compare (optional, run-on-demand or nightly for candidate changes): for PRs with marginal fast-path signals, run a longer slice-aware shadow harness that compares against the canonical baseline snapshot (master at baseline commit) using probabilistic checks.

2) Oracle scoring: ensemble of signals -> confidence score (0-100):
   - Relative drop in median tokens/sec by slice (model, seq_len_bucket, batch_size).
   - p95 increase (absolute and relative) with sample-aware correction.
   - Bayesian online changepoint detector over time-series of tokens/sec samples to reduce sensitivity to single noisy runs.
   - Lightweight effect size + posterior probability thresholding to trade false positive vs detection sensitivity.

3) Slicing and baselines:
   - Precompute slices that matter for product workload (seq len quartiles, common model families, batch sizes). Each slice has a rolling baseline distribution stored in S3 (artifact) with metadata (commit, hardware tag, kernel flags). Baseline snapshots are versioned and stored per release.

4) PR UX: GitHub check with compact summary and links: quick verdict (Pass/Warn/Fail), confidence score, top 3 slices contributing to alert, link to replay artifact and full bench dashboard. Auto-comment on PR with suggested follow-ups if Fail.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Sample size vs latency: small microbench reduces PR blocking time but increases variance. We mitigate via ensemble + conservative thresholds and a shadow extended run option.
- Cost: use preemptible/spot GPU workers for fast path; cap runs per PR/week to limit cost.
- Complexity: adopting Bayesian changepoint detection adds complexity but substantially reduces noisy false positives vs pure percentiles.

Operational guardrails:
- Circuit breaker: more than X failing PRs in a short window triggers temporary relax of thresholds and notifies oncall.
- TTL for baselines: baselines older than 30 days are invalidated and require nightly recalibration.
- Audit log: store every PR run's artifacts (trace, metrics, seed) for forensics and eval.

Deliverables:
- Mini-seed corpus + runner in the CI agent (Docker + small GPU job).
- Oracle service that ingests run metrics, compares to baseline, computes score, and posts GitHub check.
- Dashboard with historical false-positive/true-positive tracking and per-slice performance charts.

Links to artifacts and design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Benchmark+Oracle (design spec), https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-oracle (proto repo), https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/oracle (dashboard).
acceptance_criteria: Fast microbench added to PR CI that runs in <= 2 minutes and returns tokens/sec and p95 metrics
Oracle computes confidence score and posts GitHub check with Pass/Warn/Fail and slice-level diffs
Shadow extended run can be triggered from PR UI and completes within <= 25 minutes
Baseline snapshot format and S3 storage versioning implemented; CI can fetch matching baseline by release tag
False positive rate measured on historical PR corpus is <= 5% after one tuning cycle
Operational docs for oncall and cost guardrails are published
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spike completed. Verified that a 40s mini-seed run can reproducibly surface a 30% tokens/sec regression in local infra.
2026-03-04: Chose Bayesian online changepoint detector (scikit-like lightweight impl) over fixed percentile delta after A/B spike test; provides better noise tolerance on short traces.
2026-03-06: Prototype CI job implemented in bench-oracle repo; uses spot g4dn small instance; average wall time 85s in CI env (needs tuning).
2026-03-09: UX review with PM (A. Patel) and Design (R. Gomez) — added confidence score and top-3-slice rationale in PR checks; agreed to auto-comment only on Fail with mitigation hints.
2026-03-11: Ran prototype against last 500 merged PRs (replay) — identified 7 known regressions and 3 new noisy failures. Next: tighten slice bucketing and add a per-slice min-sample threshold.
decision_log: Picked two-tier run strategy to balance PR latency and sensitivity (fast synthetic + optional extended).
Adopt Bayesian detection to reduce flakiness on 30–120s runs; ensemble with effect-size threshold to keep interpretability.
Baseline snapshots will be tagged by runtime-release and kernel flags to avoid false alerts due to intentional kernel changes.
